data.title: Mammalian cell size is controlled by mTOR and its downstream targets S6K1 and 4EBP1/eIF4E
data.authors: Fingar DC; Salama S; Tsou C; Harlow E; Blenis J

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: mTOR controls mammalian cell size through its downstream translational targets S6K1 and 4E-BP1/eIF4E.
data.abstract_excerpt: The coordinated action of cell cycle progression and cell growth (an increase in cell size and cell mass) is critical for sustained cellular proliferation, yet the biochemical signals that control cell growth are poorly defined, particularly in mammalian systems. We find that cell growth and cell cycle progression are separable processes in mammalian cells and that growth to appropriate cell size requires mTOR- and PI3K-dependent signals.
